q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer
- Measured: ROAS (product net ROAS, allocated) rose while net profit (P&L net profit) got worse because the business’s contribution margin fell enough to more than offset the small improvement in ad efficiency. In plain terms: each rupee of ad now returns slightly more profit-attributed revenue, but overall contribution fell and ad spend ticked up, so the bottom-line loss widened.

Key evidence (previous → current)
- Product net ROAS (allocated): 0.73x → 0.80x (+10%) — Measured (diagnose result).
- Net profit (order_pnl.Net profit): ₹-35,790 → ₹-60,859 (loss widened by ₹25,069) — Measured (order_pnl).
- Contribution margin (order_pnl.Contribution margin): ₹333,755 → ₹314,280 (−₹19,475) — Measured.
- P&L ad spend (ad spend (P&L basis)): ₹369,545 → ₹375,138 (+₹5,594) — Measured.
- Commerce net sales: ₹641,932 → ₹525,091 (down) — Measured.
- Net COGS (order_pnl/net COGS): ₹236,553 → ₹194,999 (down) — Measured.

Why this can happen (bridge + interpretation)
- Accounting identity (measured): Net profit = contribution margin − ad spend (P&L basis).
- Measured bridge: Contribution margin fell by ₹19,475 and P&L ad spend rose by ₹5,594 → combined change ≈ −₹25,069, which matches the net profit deterioration. (Measured.)
- ROAS rose because ad-attributed profitability per rupee improved (product net ROAS (allocated) up; platform-level gains on Meta / IG_feed were noted) — Measured. However the business sold less (net sales and orders declined) and allocated product-level profit fell, so total contribution dropped — Measured. Those two effects together explain why ROAS↑ but net profit↓. (Derived + Measured.)
- Hypothesis (not proven): the ROAS gain looks driven by mix/targeting (better-performing campaigns or regions) while an overall fall in order volume, product mix or promo changes reduced total contribution. Returns, discounts and AOV may also matter but need verification.

What remains unverified / recommended next steps
- Unverified: campaign / product-level contributors to the contribution drop (which campaigns improved ROAS but reduced P&L), AOV movement, and whether returns/discounts or taxes drove the contribution fall (some tax metrics failed to fetch).
- Next steps I can run now: drill the net profit change by product and ad platform, or run a diagnose on net profit with campaign and product drivers to surface likely causes. Which would you like: "Break down the net profit change by ad platform and top 10 campaigns" or "Show product-level contribution vs product-level ROAS"?
